brief.headline: Blackstone Mortgage Trust Reports $327.6M Loss as It Cuts Older Office Loans
bullets: Earnings & AUM: Blackstone Mortgage Trust (BXMT) reported a net loss of $327.6 million in income in the third quarter of 2026, a roughly fourfold increase from second-quarter losses.

Exits & Secondaries: Carlyle Group and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development have agreed to sell Black Sea Oil & Gas, a Romanian offshore gas producer supplying around 10% of the country’s gas needs, to Mazarine Energy, according to a report by Reuters.
Insurance & Retirement: About 52% of people with a workplace retirement plan say they would invest in private assets if they were available in their company’s plan.

Private Credit: Blue Owl Capital has reported a decline in redemption requests at its flagship private credit fund for the second consecutive quarter, as investor demand for withdrawals continued to ease in Q3.
People & Leadership: Jason Maurer has joined SL Green Realty, Manhattan’s largest office landlord, as a managing director.
brief.marketRead: Bottom line: calm volatility and open credit markets are a supportive backdrop for dealmaking, fundraising and exits. The S&P 500 stands at 7,720.39 (down 0.3% on the prior reading) and the VIX is 17.2, a normal-volatility reading. The effective fed funds rate is 3.88%, the 10-year Treasury yield is 5.05% (up 6 bps on the prior reading) and the 10Y–2Y yield curve is +0.37 pts (positively sloped). High-yield credit spreads are 3.26%, near long-run norms (up 12 bps on the prior reading).

items.title: Blue Owl private credit redemption requests fall again in Q3
items.takeaway: Blue Owl Capital has reported a decline in redemption requests at its flagship private credit fund for the second consecutive quarter, as investor demand for withdrawals continued to ease in Q3.
items.whyItMatters: Fewer withdrawal requests suggest investors are growing more comfortable with private credit, which eases pressure on managers to sell assets to pay them out.
items.marketContext: The effective fed funds rate is 3.88% and high-yield credit spreads are 3.26%, near long-run norms (up 12 bps on the prior reading). Most private loans pay a floating rate, so lender income tracks short-term rates while spreads show how much extra investors demand for credit risk. (FRED data as of Oct 29.)

beginnerNote.explanation: Loans made by investment funds rather than banks, usually to mid-sized companies. They often pay higher, floating interest rates.
